decides: Account foundation: features enabled, fiscal calendar, subsidiaries, base currencies, module list
costOfChange: Severe - several features cannot be disabled at all, or only via NetSuite Support
fedByRaw: SYS-5, SYS-7, FIN-1, FIN-2, FIN-3c, FIN-4, FIN-5a, FIN-6, FIN-7, DIM-6, ITM-2, ITM-3, ITM-5, ITM-6, QLT-2, P2P-5, O2C-5, O2C-6, ORG-7
notes: Enable nothing speculatively. Every feature here should trace to a documented business need. Enable Multi-Location Inventory BEFORE loading items and before the first period you intend to open.

decides: Structure: chart of accounts, department, class, location, custom segments, accounting preferences, period locking
costOfChange: High - adding a dimension later cannot retroactively tag history
fedByRaw: DIM-1 to DIM-8, FIN-4, FIN-8, ITM-5, CLS-10
notes: The most common Excel-to-ERP failure is rebuilding dimension logic inside account names.

decides: Master data: items, costing method per item, lot designation, BOMs, vendors, customers, pricing, roles
costOfChange: Mixed - costing method and lot designation are one-way; GL mapping is not
fedByRaw: ITM-1, ITM-3, ITM-4, ITM-6, ITM-7, ITM-8, ITM-10, SYS-2, SYS-8, P2P-3, O2C-1, O2C-8, ORG-1
notes: Item load is the single highest-risk migration step. Dry-run it in sandbox more than once.

decides: Transaction flows: procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, production, quality disposition, inventory movement
costOfChange: Moderate - process and form changes are recoverable
fedByRaw: P2P-1 to P2P-13, O2C-2, O2C-4, O2C-9, ITM-5, ITM-6, ITM-11, QLT-4
notes: Configure against the real process from the packet, including the workarounds.

decides: Controls: approval routing, permissions, segregation of duties, close-prep saved searches
notes: Build the close-prep saved searches early. They shorten the first close, not the tenth.

decides: Integrations: A/P platform, TMS, subscription platform, marketplaces, EDI, payment processors, everything in SYS-4
costOfChange: Low to moderate - depends on the connector
fedByRaw: P2P-8, O2C-3, O2C-5, O2C-6, O2C-7, O2C-10, CSH-2, CSH-3, SYS-4, SYS-6
notes: Decide per system: does it originate transactions in NetSuite, or does NetSuite reconcile to it?

decides: Reporting: financial statement layouts, saved searches, dashboards, KPIs, traceability test
costOfChange: Low to rebuild - BUT high if it proves the L1 dimensions were wrong
fedByRaw: CLS-8, RPT-1 to RPT-3, DIM-3, QLT-6
notes: Build the day-one reports during UAT, not after go-live. They are the real test of L1. Run a mock recall against the system as the traceability acceptance test.

decides: Cutover: opening balances, open transactions, inventory, reconciliation, go-live date
costOfChange: Very high - a bad cutover is the most common post-go-live fire drill

notes: Opening balances that do not tie are the single most common post-migration problem.
